transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Torres (Cascade Head of ML), Sam Wilson (CTO), Priya Rao (Platform Eng), Omar Li (SRE)

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'll kick off, this is Maya from Redwood, with Ravi our SE. can you each do a quick intro?
00:07 Elena Torres: yeah hi I'm elena, head of ml at Cascade, we're building a multi-lingual summarization and extraction pipeline for legal docs, lots of long context.
00:15 Sam Wilson: Sam, CTO, evaluating infra and cost - main asks are latency under 300ms for short queries and ability to do 32k context for document summarization jobs.
00:25 Priya Rao: Priya, platform eng - focused on deployment model, VPC, SSO, and KMS integration.
00:32 Maya Chen: great, thanks. quick agenda: model selection questions (open model comparsions, context length, multilingual, tool-calling), hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private), security, and next steps. sound good?
00:44 Sam Wilson: yep
00:46 Ravi Patel: quick note, i'll talk about perf and latency tradeoffs and batching, and also explain quant profiles for dedicated GPUs.
00:55 Elena Torres: perfect. Our current stack: a mix of internal infra and GCP, we use embeddings from another vendor but want to move generation in-house. Are Redwood models single-tenant? how do you handle model versions?
01:10 Maya Chen: good q. For hosted we run multi-tenant but you can pin model versions; Dedicated is your reserved GPU pool - effectively single-tenant for inference. Private deploy is customer-controlled. model catalog includes curated open models (Redwood-verified profiles) and we also host some tuned variants.
01:28 Elena Torres: regarding models — we need a 32k context model for chunked doc summarization, plus a faster 4k/8k option for chat. we're also multi-lingual: EN, ES, FR, PT, and occasional JA. which open models do you recommend?
01:45 Ravi Patel: empirically for long context we point customers at Llama 3 large 32k variants and mix in Claude-style families for instruction tuning; for multilingual capability, mT5-ish or Mistral multilingual forks can help. caveat, names may be off in transcript but the idea is choose a model with good tokenization for those languages. we also offer quantized variants to reduce cost.
02:10 Sam Wilson: any issues with tool-calling / function calling? we need to call internal APIs and pass structured responses back.
02:18 Ravi Patel: yes, function-calling is supported at the Redwood API layer for hosted and dedicated; for private we ship the same runtime so RPCs look the same. there are slight differences: hosted has managed tool-call routing and sanitizer hooks, Dedicated gives you more control on timeouts and concurrency.
02:36 Elena Torres: latency — for our interactive UI we need median under 300ms for short prompts, can that be done on dedicated?
02:44 Ravi Patel: depends on payload size and batching. for small prompts on dedicated with optimized kernels and smaller model variants you can hit <200ms median. key is plan for autoscale headroom and low-concurrency paths to avoid cross-request batching add. 
03:00 Maya Chen: cost perspective — Hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable throughput and often cheaper per-token at scale. Private has licensing/ops costs. we'll share a sizing spreadsheet.
03:18 Priya Rao: security — SOC2 and audit logs are musts, also SSO/SAML and customer-managed KMS for keys. do you provide audit logs per-token or per-request?
03:29 Maya Chen: we provide request-level audit logs and integration with KMS/HSM for private deployments, hosted supports envelope encryption and customer-managed keys in certain tiers. we'll include our security docs (link).
03:42 Sam Wilson: regarding tokenization, do open models handle multilingual well or do we need language-specific models? we've seen hallucination on Spanish legal abbreviations.
03:52 Ravi Patel: tokenization varies; sometimes using a multilingual model with good subword coverage helps, but for legal domain you may need domain-adapted vocab or fine-tuning. another approach is pretoken normalization or language detection + route to language-optimized model.
04:10 Elena Torres: tool-call output — we need structured JSON responses reliably. how do you ensure parsable outputs?
04:18 Ravi Patel: we recommend function calling with strict schemas and validation in the application layer. on Dedicated we can enable stricter decoding constraints and n-best reranking. also we have an eval harness to validate structure across prompts.
04:34 Maya Chen: quick note, many customers use a small hybrid architecture: Hosted for low-friction chat proofs, Dedicated for production inference, and Private for regulated workloads.
04:45 Priya Rao: latency vs cost tradeoffs — curious about batching. If we batch aggressively we save cost but hurt tail latency. are there tuning knobs?
04:55 Ravi Patel: yes, Redwood has workload-aware batching configs and a latency SLO routing policy. we can pin some routes to low-batch fast-paths and others to high-efficiency batch queues.
05:10 Sam Wilson: can you run our prompt set for a benchmark? we'd send 1000 prompts with mix of 512-token and 20k-token contexts.
05:18 Maya Chen: yes, that's exactly what we do for model selection. Ravi will run a small internal bench and then we can do a 1:1 run on Dedicated.
05:26 Elena Torres: any gotchas migrating from SageMaker endpoints? we currently host a custom model there.
05:33 Ravi Patel: migration is pretty standard: model weights + config, then we tune quantization profiles. differences in runtime calls and kv cache handling are the main engineering work. sometimes proprietary runtime ops need small adaptors.
05:50 Maya Chen: ok, let's capture action items — we'll send pricing and Dedicated sizing. Ravi will share benchmark notes and sample prompts. Cascade will prepare prompt set and token distribution.
06:00 Priya Rao: also we'll need SSO metadata and your SOC2 certs to initiate legal review.
06:07 Maya Chen: we'll attach SOC2 docs and SSO instructions.
06:12 Omar Li: quick ops Q — for private/on-prem do you support air-gapped installs?
06:18 Ravi Patel: yes we support on-prem package for air-gapped installs, though it requires additional ops lead time and a support plan.
06:25 Sam Wilson: timeline — we want a POC in 3 weeks, pilot in 6-8 weeks. is that realistic?
06:31 Maya Chen: POC in 3 weeks is doable if we get prompt set and access; Dedicated sizing and pricing within a week.
06:40 Elena Torres: ok great. thanks everyone.
06:44 Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet, security docs, and schedule the cost workshop. notes: links - pricing spreadsheet (drive link), security packet (link), model comparison deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/model-selection.pdf)
06:58 Transcript notes: transcription has a few errors on model names and acronyms, some speaker labels merged.

(End of transcript)
